Spain isn't one flag pretending to be one country — it's several. This map is every region with a real, organized push to leave, and two of them have already tried it for real.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ Catalonia went furthest. On 1 October 2017 it held a referendum Spain's Constitutional Court had already suspended; police were sent to stop voting. Catalan officials reported about 90% in favor on roughly 43% turnout.
2/ On 27 October 2017 Catalonia's parliament voted 70–10 to declare independence. Madrid answered within hours by invoking Article 155, dissolving the Catalan government and imposing direct rule.
3/ President Carles Puigdemont and four ministers fled into exile rather than face arrest. Snap elections that December still returned a pro-independence majority — just a smaller one.

4/ The Basque Country's movement turned violent for decades. ETA, founded in 1959, killed roughly 829 people — about 340 of them civilians — before finally surrendering its weapons in 2017 and dissolving completely in 2018.
5/ Galicia, Andalusia and the Canary and Balearic Islands all have their own nationalist movements too, just quieter ones — mostly pushing for more autonomy rather than a break from Madrid.
6/ Same country, at least half a dozen separate arguments about what 'Spain' even is. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
